deep.reconstruction:
SETTING (from the neighbouring pages). Four-dimensional Euclidean space has coordinates x, y, a, b, which can also be read as C^2 with complex coordinates x+iy and a+ib. It is parametrised by two pairs of parameters, (p,q) (called xi, eta on the next page; polar form p = r cos phi, q = r sin phi on the previous page) and (alpha, beta). Two kinds of condition are imposed:
(i) the (p,q)-surfaces and the (alpha,beta)-surfaces are mutually orthogonal;
(ii) each family is conformally parametrised.
The previous page writes (ii) as x_p - i y_p = y_q + i x_q and a_p - i b_p = b_q + i a_q. In the metric this gives
ds^2 = E (dp^2 + dq^2) + G (dalpha^2 + dbeta^2),
with E = x_p^2 + y_p^2 + a_p^2 + b_p^2 and G = x_alpha^2 + y_alpha^2 + a_alpha^2 + b_alpha^2 (next page). The aim, judging by the second half of this page, is potential theory for this 4-dimensional metric.

PART 1: algebra of the orthogonality conditions.
(1) Real orthogonality conditions:
x_alpha x_p + y_alpha y_p + a_alpha a_p + b_alpha b_p = 0,
x_beta x_p + y_beta y_p + ... = 0 (second line; see corrections).
(2) These are packed into one complex equation:
(x_alpha + i y_alpha)(x_p - i y_p) + (a_alpha + i b_alpha)(a_p - i b_p) = 0.
Its real part is the alpha-p dot product. Its imaginary part, x_p y_alpha - y_p x_alpha + a_p b_alpha - b_p a_alpha, becomes (up to sign) the beta-p or alpha-q dot product once the conformality relations are used [my gloss].
(3) Dividing gives (x_p - i y_p)/(a_p - i b_p) = -(a_alpha + i b_alpha)/(x_alpha + i y_alpha). The right side does not depend on whether p or q is used. Hence
(x_p - i y_p)/(a_p - i b_p) = (x_q - i y_q)/(a_q - i b_q) =: L + M i.
(4) Multiplying the p-relation by the conjugate of the q-relation:
(x_p - i y_p)(x_q + i y_q) = (L^2 + M^2)(a_p - i b_p)(a_q + i b_q).
Riemann writes this with the roles of the (x,y) and (a,b) factors exchanged (see errors).
(5) Real parts: a_p a_q + b_p b_q is a positive multiple of x_p x_q + y_p y_q. Conformality of the (p,q)-parametrisation makes the full 4D sum vanish. Since the multiple is positive, each part vanishes separately:
a_p a_q + b_p b_q = 0 and x_p x_q + y_p y_q = 0.
This is the last line of the top block. The next page completes the argument: the ratio is both holomorphic and antiholomorphic, hence constant ('q.e.a.').

PART 2: potential theory in the 4-metric, behaviour near the surface p = q = 0.
(6) Volume element sqrt(det g) = E G. The Dirichlet integral is
D(u) = ∫ [ (u_p^2 + u_q^2) G + (u_alpha^2 + u_beta^2) E ] dp dq dalpha dbeta,
which is the integral line on the page. The Laplace-Beltrami equation [mine, implied] is
d_p(G u_p) + d_q(G u_q) + d_alpha(E u_alpha) + d_beta(E u_beta) = 0.
(7) Flux through the tube r = const around the 2-surface p = q = 0, using polar p,q:
∫ du/dn dS = ∫ u_r r G dphi dalpha dbeta.
This follows because the normal derivative is u_r/sqrt(E) and the area element of the tube is sqrt(E) r G dphi dalpha dbeta. Riemann writes ∂u/∂p (crossed) or ∂u/(r∂r) on the left; the correct integrand is u_r r G.
(8) A crossed-out attempt writes the equation in polar form:
( (1/r) d_r(r u_r) + (1/r^2) u_phiphi ) G + (u_alphaalpha + u_betabeta) E + u_alpha d_alpha E + ...
(9) Local expansion near p = q = 0:
x = x_0 + x_p p + x_q q,
so G ≈ Σ (x_alpha + x_{p alpha} p + x_{q alpha} q)^2. The equation becomes
(u_pp + u_qq) G + u_p d_p G + u_q d_q G + (u_alphaalpha + u_betabeta) E + (alpha, beta first-order terms) = 0,
with d_p G = 2 Σ x_{alpha p}(x_alpha + ...) and so on, exactly as in the three bracketed lines.
(10) For a solution singular like log r along the surface: u_p = cos(phi)/r and u_q = sin(phi)/r. The first-order terms are therefore (A cos phi + B sin phi)/r with A = d_p G and B = d_q G at r = 0. The last two (faint) lines set the correcting terms equal to A cos phi + B sin phi, i.e. they determine the next term in the singular expansion. That term is of type r log r (A' cos phi + B' sin phi) [my gloss]. The page breaks off there.
errors: Step (4) as written, (a_p - i b_p)(a_q + i b_q) = (LL+MM)(x_p - i y_p)(x_q + i y_q), inverts the factor. With L+Mi defined as (x-part)/(a-part), the correct relation is (x_p - i y_p)(x_q + i y_q) = (L^2+M^2)(a_p - i b_p)(a_q + i b_q). This is harmless for the conclusion, since only the positivity of the factor is used.
Flux formula: the left side is written with ∂u/∂p (or ∂u/(r∂r)), and the factor r appears again on the right. The consistent flux is ∫ u_r r G dphi dalpha dbeta. This is a notational slip.
In the crossed-out polar Laplacian, the term ∂((1/r)∂u/∂phi)/∂phi lacks a 1/r (it should be (1/r^2) u_phiphi). It is cancelled by Riemann anyway.
The last two lines are fragmentary and faint. Their exact coefficients cannot be checked; the derivation is unfinished.

results.what: Packing the real orthogonality conditions between two conformally parametrised surface families in R^4 = C^2 into one complex equation. Deducing that the ratio (x_p - i y_p)/(a_p - i b_p) is independent of direction, and that each complex coordinate pair is separately orthogonal.
results.modern_name: Hermitian inner product on C^2 / orthogonal nets of complex (or anti-complex) curves; rigidity of such orthogonal conformal nets
results.usually_credited_to: No specific attribution; elementary differential geometry of surfaces in R^4 (later systematic work on surfaces in E^4 by Kommerell, Eisenhart, etc.)

results.what: Dirichlet integral and Laplace-Beltrami operator for the metric E(dp^2+dq^2)+G(dalpha^2+dbeta^2) on 4-space.
results.modern_name: Laplace-Beltrami operator / Dirichlet energy in orthogonal coordinates

results.what: Flux through a tubular neighbourhood of a codimension-2 surface, and a local expansion of a solution with logarithmic singularity along that surface, with first-order correction terms of the form A cos phi + B sin phi.
results.modern_name: Asymptotic expansion of a Green-type function singular along a codimension-2 submanifold (log-singularity, tubular-neighbourhood analysis)
results.usually_credited_to: Generally associated with later potential theory (e.g. singular solutions along curves and surfaces; Hadamard-style parametrix constructions, early 20th c.)

deep.surprise_reason: Most of the page is routine: complex packing of orthogonality relations, and a Dirichlet integral and Laplacian in orthogonal coordinates. The mildly interesting element is the attempt to build a 4-dimensional potential with logarithmic singularity along a 2-surface, using a tubular-neighbourhood flux and a polar expansion. This fits Riemann's known 1850s interest in potential theory and the Dirichlet principle, possibly in a several-complex-variables setting. It is fragmentary and unfinished and contains no completed result.

checkable.sympy: xa,ya,aa,ba,xp,yp,ap,bp=symbols('xa ya aa ba xp yp ap bp',real=True); simplify(re(expand((xa+I*ya)*(xp-I*yp)+(aa+I*ba)*(ap-I*bp))) - (xa*xp+ya*yp+aa*ap+ba*bp))
checkable.asserts: The real part of the complex packing equals the 4D dot product of the alpha- and p-tangent vectors (result 0).

checkable.sympy: L,M,ap,bp,aq,bq=symbols('L M ap bp aq bq',real=True); Xp=(L+I*M)*(ap-I*bp); Xq=(L+I*M)*(aq-I*bq); simplify(expand(Xp*conjugate(Xq) - (L**2+M**2)*(ap-I*bp)*(aq+I*bq)))
checkable.asserts: If x_p - i y_p = (L+iM)(a_p - i b_p) and likewise for q, then (x_p - i y_p)(x_q + i y_q) = (L^2+M^2)(a_p - i b_p)(a_q + i b_q). This is the corrected form of Riemann's line (result 0).

checkable.sympy: r,phi=symbols('r phi',positive=True); u=Function('u'); p=r*cos(phi); q=r*sin(phi); U=log(r); simplify(diff(U,r,2)+diff(U,r)/r+diff(U,phi,2)/r**2)
checkable.asserts: log r is harmonic in the (p,q)-plane via the polar Laplacian u_rr + u_r/r + u_phiphi/r^2 (result 0).
The correction term (r log r /2) cos phi solves Δv = cos(phi)/r, the type of first-order term (A cos phi + B sin phi)/r arising from u = log r (result 0).

checkable.sympy: p,q,al,be=symbols('p q alpha beta'); E=Function('E')(p,q,al,be); G=Function('G')(p,q,al,be); u=Function('u')(p,q,al,be); g=diag(E,E,G,G); sq=sqrt(g.det()); simplify(sq - E*G)
checkable.asserts: The volume element of ds^2 = E(dp^2+dq^2) + G(dalpha^2+dbeta^2) is E*G, so the Dirichlet integral is ∫[G(u_p^2+u_q^2)+E(u_alpha^2+u_beta^2)] dp dq dalpha dbeta (result 0, assuming E,G > 0).

transcription_corrections: Line 2 is not 'x_p x_p + y_p y_p ... = 0' (a sum of squares cannot vanish). The image reads approximately ∂x/∂β ∂x/∂p + ∂y/∂β ∂y/∂p ... = 0, the second orthogonality condition.
In the Dirichlet-integral line the first factor should be read as (u_p^2 + u_q^2). The sign shown as '-' in the transcription is doubtful; only a plus makes sense for the Dirichlet integral.
The end of the integral line reads ∂p ∂q (written above a cancelled ∂α∂β/∂φ), i.e. the full measure is dp dq dalpha dbeta.
The flux line: the left side is ∫ ∂u/∂r ... dS (the first symbol is overwritten), and the right side is ∂u/∂r · r · (x_alpha^2 + y_alpha^2 + a_alpha^2 + b_alpha^2) ∂phi ∂alpha ∂beta.
Riemann writes the L and M symbols as script/Gothic letters; the transcription's \mathfrak{L}, \mathfrak{M} is acceptable.
The last two lines are very faint. The reading '(A cos phi + B sin phi)' and '... = A cos phi + B sin phi' is plausible, but the intermediate terms are uncertain.
